title: Rivers
source: After the notes' South America and Africa physical maps, with standard UPSC facts added

places.name: Amazon

source.name: Mantaro
source.significance: Where the river of the selvas rises: a river of the Andes of central Peru, flowing out of Lake Junín

places.significance: The river of the selvas, the world's largest rainforest — second longest on Earth, and the greatest of all by the water it carries
notes: Flows through Peru, Colombia and Brazil
Rises in the Andes of Peru as the **Mantaro**
The second longest river in the world, after the Nile — and the largest by width and volume
Its largest tributary is the **Madeira**
Reaches the Atlantic at **Macapá**, on the Equator
Drains the Amazon forest — the selvas, the world's largest evergreen rainforest

places.name: Madeira
places.significance: The largest tributary of the river of the selvas, formed on the Bolivian border and running north-east past Porto Velho
notes: The Amazon's largest tributary
Formed where the Mamoré and the Beni meet, on the Brazil–Bolivia border

places.name: Macapá
places.significance: The city at the mouth of the world's greatest river, standing on the Equator
notes: Marks the Amazon's mouth on the Atlantic
Capital of Brazil's Amapá state

places.name: Magdalena

source.name: Laguna de la Magdalena
source.significance: Where Colombia's great river rises, a small lake high in the Colombian Massif, where the Andes part into three ranges

places.significance: Colombia's chief river, running north between the Andes' cordilleras to the Caribbean at Barranquilla
notes: Flows through Colombia
Mouth: the **Caribbean Sea**, at Bocas de Ceniza by Barranquilla

places.name: Orinoco

source.name: Cerro Delgado Chalbaud
source.significance: Where Venezuela's great river rises, on a peak of the highlands along the Brazilian border

places.significance: Venezuela's great river, arcing round the Guiana Highlands and across the grasslands of the Llanos to a delta on the Atlantic
notes: Flows through Venezuela, and along its border with Colombia
Drains the **Llanos** grasslands
Its basin holds **Angel Falls**, the highest waterfall in the world

places.name: Angel Falls
places.significance: The highest waterfall in the world, plunging 979 m off a tabletop mountain in Canaima National Park
notes: The world's highest uninterrupted waterfall: 979 m (3,212 ft)
Falls from Auyán-tepui, on a stream that drains through the Caroní to the Orinoco

places.name: Paraná

source.name: Brazilian Highlands
source.significance: Where South America's second river rises, as the Rio Grande in the Serra da Mantiqueira of Minas Gerais

places.significance: South America's second river, from the Brazilian Highlands past Paraguay into Argentina — dammed at Itaipu, it ends in the Río de la Plata
notes: Flows through Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina
Rises in the **Brazilian Highlands**
Mouth: the **Río de la Plata**
**Itaipu**, on the Brazil–Paraguay border, is the largest dam of South America

places.name: Itaipu Dam
places.significance: The largest dam of South America, on the Brazil–Paraguay border just above the meeting point with Argentina
notes: Shared by Brazil and Paraguay
One of the world's largest hydroelectric plants

places.name: Río de la Plata
places.significance: The broad estuary between Buenos Aires and Montevideo into which South America's second river empties
notes: Mouth of the Paraná (and the Uruguay)

places.name: Nile
places.significance: The longest river on Earth, flowing north through the desert from Khartoum to a delta on the Mediterranean — Egypt's lifeline
notes: The longest river in the world, about 6,650 km
Formed at **Khartoum**, where the **White Nile** and the **Blue Nile** meet
Dammed at **Aswan**: the High Dam holds back **Lake Nasser**
Flows past **Cairo** into its delta, the Rosetta branch reaching the sea by **Alexandria** port
Flows through Sudan and Egypt to the Mediterranean

places.name: White Nile

source.name: Jinja
source.significance: Where the longer headstream leaves Africa's largest lake, at the Ugandan town on its northern shore

places.significance: The longer headstream, leaving Africa's largest lake at Jinja and winding through Uganda and the Sudd swamps to Khartoum
notes: Rises at **Lake Victoria**, leaving it at Jinja, Uganda
Passes through Lake Kyoga and **Lake Albert**
Crosses the **Sudd**, the vast swamp of South Sudan
Meets the Blue Nile at **Khartoum**: from there the river is the Nile

places.name: Blue Nile

source.name: Bahir Dar
source.significance: Where the shorter headstream leaves Ethiopia's largest lake, by the city on its southern shore

places.significance: The shorter headstream that brings most of the water and silt, leaving Ethiopia's largest lake through a deep gorge to Khartoum
notes: Rises at **Lake Tana**, Ethiopia — called the Abay there
Brings most of the Nile's water, and the silt of its floods
Dammed by the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD)
Meets the White Nile at **Khartoum**: from there the river is the Nile

places.name: Niger

source.name: Guinea Highlands
source.significance: Where West Africa's great river rises, in the hills by the Sierra Leone border, some 240 km from the Atlantic

places.significance: West Africa's great river, rising only 240 km from the Atlantic yet flowing away from it in a boomerang arc through Mali to a vast delta on the Gulf of Guinea
notes: Flows through Guinea, Mali, Niger and Nigeria
Rises in the **Guinea Highlands**, only about 240 km from the Atlantic, yet flows inland first
Its largest tributary is the **Benue**, joining at Lokoja
Ends in the oil-rich **Niger Delta**, by **Port Harcourt**
Floods an inland delta in Mali every year

places.name: Benue
places.significance: The largest tributary of West Africa's great river, rising in northern Cameroon and joining it at Lokoja
notes: Rises in northern Cameroon, on the Adamawa Plateau
Joins the Niger at **Lokoja**, Nigeria — its largest tributary

places.name: Congo

source.name: Musofi
source.significance: Where the river of the central rainforest rises as the Lualaba, on the copper plateau of the DRC's far south-east

places.significance: The deepest river on Earth, crossing the Equator twice in a great arc through the rainforest of central Africa
notes: The deepest river in the world — over 220 m
Flows through the DRC and along the border of the Republic of the Congo — also known as the **Zaire**
Cuts the **Equator twice**
Rises as the **Lualaba**; below the **Stanley (Boyoma) Falls** it is the Congo
Home of the **Pygmy** tribe, in its forests
Second only to the Amazon in the water it carries

places.name: Zambezi

source.name: Kalene Hill
source.significance: Where southern Africa's great eastward river rises, in north-west Zambia near the Angola and DRC borders

places.significance: Africa's fourth-longest river, flowing east from north-west Zambia over Mosi-oa-Tunya and through two great reservoirs to the Indian Ocean
notes: Zambia — Zambezi: it rises in north-west Zambia
Rises near the **Katanga Plateau**, by the borders of Angola and the DRC
Plunges over **Victoria Falls**
Dammed at **Kariba**, holding back Lake Kariba
Flows through Zambia and Angola, along the Namibia, Botswana and Zimbabwe borders, and through Mozambique to the Indian Ocean

places.name: Orange

source.name: Mont-aux-Sources
source.significance: Where South Africa's longest river rises, high on Lesotho's border with KwaZulu-Natal

places.significance: South Africa's longest river, rising in the mountains of Lesotho and flowing west across the plateau to the Atlantic
notes: Forms a natural border between **South Africa** and **Namibia**
Rises in Lesotho, where it is called the Senqu
Flows west to the Atlantic

places.name: Limpopo

source.name: Witwatersrand
source.significance: Where the river rises as the Crocodile, on the gold-bearing ridge of Johannesburg

places.significance: The river that bounds South Africa against Botswana and Zimbabwe, crossing the Tropic of Capricorn on its way to the Indian Ocean
notes: Forms South Africa's border with **Botswana** and **Zimbabwe**
Cuts the **Tropic of Capricorn** — twice
Drains into the **Indian Ocean**, in Mozambique
Rises as the Crocodile River on the Witwatersrand

places.name: Khartoum
places.significance: Where the two headstreams meet and the great river begins, at Sudan's capital
notes: Meeting point of the **White Nile** and the **Blue Nile** — the Mogran

places.name: Aswan High Dam
places.significance: The great dam that ended the river's floods in Egypt in 1970, holding back a reservoir across the Sudan border
notes: On the Nile, in Egypt
Holds back **Lake Nasser** (man-made)

places.name: Cairo
places.significance: Egypt's capital, at the head of the delta, where the great river begins to divide
notes: Capital of Egypt
Where the Nile divides into its delta

places.name: Alexandria
places.significance: Egypt's great Mediterranean port, at the delta's western edge
notes: Egypt's chief port, on the Mediterranean

places.name: Port Harcourt
places.significance: The oil port of the delta's eastern side, on the Bonny river
notes: Nigeria's chief oil port, in the Niger Delta

places.name: Boyoma Falls
places.significance: Seven cataracts over 100 km of the river above Kisangani — by the volume of water the largest falls on Earth
notes: On the Congo (Lualaba), above Kisangani
Once called the Stanley Falls

places.name: Victoria Falls
places.significance: The 'smoke that thunders': the largest sheet of falling water on Earth, 1.7 km wide, on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border
notes: On the Zambezi, between Zambia and Zimbabwe
Called Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders'

places.name: Kariba Dam
places.significance: The dam on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border that holds back the world's largest reservoir by volume
notes: On the Zambezi, completed in 1959
Holds back Lake Kariba

groups.name: Paraná — its countries
groups.mnemonic: Pa·ra·na — Para for Paraguay, ra for Brazil, na for Argentina

groups.name: Magdalena
groups.mnemonic: Nadi — Mug Daal lena: the Magdalena
